questions.explain: The ADE mental model runs on three axes: confidence bounds (confidence score, risk classification, authorized scope per action), reversibility tiers (Tier 1 immediate, Tier 2 recoverable, Tier 3 destructive), and observability contracts (structured audit events with triggering signal, decision logic, confidence, action, and outcome).
options: Confidence, speed, and cost
Automation rate, page volume, and ticket count
Confidence bounds, reversibility tiers, and observability contracts
CPU, memory, and storage
questions.q: What are the three axes of the ADE mental model, and what does each enforce?

questions.explain: The dispatcher's code shows: actions below the confidence threshold are SKIPPED_LOW_CONFIDENCE; Tier 3 destructive actions always route to PENDING_HUMAN_APPROVAL; Tier 2 actions need confidence of at least 0.90 to execute without approval.
options: Every action executes immediately
Below-threshold confidence is skipped, Tier 3 destructive actions always require human approval, and Tier 2 recoverable actions need confidence of at least 0.90 to auto-execute
Only Tier 1 actions are audited
Approval is requested only on failure
questions.q: How does the AutonomousDispatcher code enforce confidence and reversibility gates?

questions.explain: The canonical portfolio project is a complete five-stage autonomous loop: signal collection, anomaly detection, diagnosis (rules + LLM), dispatch (tier + confidence gate), and outcome collection — proving the competency by building a system that observes, diagnoses, decides, acts, and learns.
options: A monitoring dashboard
A manual runbook collection
An automated backup script
A five-stage autonomous loop: signal collection, anomaly detection, diagnosis, dispatch, and outcome collection
questions.q: What is the canonical first production-grade autonomous loop project recommended in the chapter?

questions.explain: The Skills Triad combines database engineering depth, platform engineering breadth (Kubernetes, IaC, CI/CD, observability, cloud primitives), and automation/AI systems design (feedback loops, signal collection, decision logic, LLM-assisted diagnosis, and classical control theory).
options: Database engineering depth, platform engineering breadth, and automation/AI systems design
SQL syntax, Excel formulas, and meeting facilitation
Networking, storage, and procurement
Python, Java, and C++ alone
questions.q: What three competency domains form the ADE Skills Triad?

questions.explain: The weekly review answers four questions: actions a human wouldn't have taken, incidents the system should have caught, false-positive rates of alert rules feeding the loop, and confidence threshold calibration — producing at least one concrete loop improvement per week.
options: It is a status meeting with management
It produces no action items
It reviews weekly autonomous actions against four questions — unexpected actions, missed incidents, false-positive rates, confidence calibration — yielding at least one concrete loop improvement
It replaces all other engineering work
questions.q: What is the weekly autonomous system review supposed to accomplish?
